references.text: The background for the Israelites gathering at Mizpah was the horrific incident involving a Levite's concubine, which led to all the tribes being summoned to discuss the matter.
The Israelites' assembly at Mizpah is described here, where the whole congregation gathered as one man before the Lord.
At Mizpah, the Israelites had sworn that no one would give his daughter in marriage to a Benjaminite, showing the seriousness of this gathering.
Mizpah was also a gathering place under Samuel, where Israel sought the Lord and confessed their sins.
Samuel called the people together at Mizpah to choose a king, demonstrating the site's significance as a meeting place for important national decisions.
A similar question about wickedness arose when the tribes confronted the Transjordan tribes over the altar, with the words 'What is this treachery?'
